title: Latency thermometry field notes — exploratory protocol
content:
Purpose / quick elevator:
Estimate how sensitive p50/p95/p99 response latency is to transient GPU memory pressure and small-context KV-cache churn. Calling this 'thermometry' — trying to measure a single axis (memory pressure + context churn) and get a sigmoid-like sensitivity curve.

Why this is different from a microburst log:
- Not focused on arrival waveform; instead we artificially inject small state changes that affect kernel selection and memory copy behavior (e.g., frequent KV cache evictions, 1–4MB context swaps).
- Goal is an operational knob: identify a threshold where we should route requests to smaller model variants or enable local CPU fallback.

Hypotheses (prior):
1) Small, repeated KV-cache evictions reduce throughput before increasing median latency — p95/p99 rise nonlinearly once eviction frequency crosses ~15 evictions/min.
2) Memory pressure that forces a split between compute kernels (float16->int8 fallbacks) creates a ~10–25% p95 penalty even if p50 remains stable.
3) Mixed-priority lanes amplify tail when lower-priority tasks evict tokenized contexts from pinned memory.

Experiment plan (short):
1) Setup: dedicated dev node with 2xA100(40GB) empty. Deploy a tiny redwood test model (open-7b-q4) with KV caching enabled.
2) Baseline run (30m): steady Poisson arrivals @ 85 qps, 16-token responses avg. Capture p50/p95/p99, and alloc/free traces.
3) Injected pressure runs: for each run (20m):
   - evict_rate = [0, 5, 10, 20, 40] evictions/min (scripted)
   - background low-priority batch jobs: size 4–8 requests/sec with long contexts (512 tokens) to force larger KV footprints
   - measure same metrics + GPU memory high-water / swap events + kernel-change counts (tracked via runtime telemetry)
4) Repeat each condition 3x for jitter estimate.

Commands / infra notes (quick):
- local harness: infra/scripts/thermo_inject.py --evict-rate <n> --bg-qps <n> --run-secs 1200
- trace collection: curl to /_telemetry/trace?run=thermo-<evict>-<trial> and gsutil cp from test-cluster:/var/logs/thermo/*
- model: redwood/open-7b-q4 pinned v2025-10-18 (small mem footprint, quantized kernels)

Prelim raw snapshot (one run, 2026-03-02, single trial):
- baseline (0 evictions/min): p50=18ms, p95=46ms, p99=120ms, avg gpu mem=23.8GB
- 10 evictions/min: p50=19ms, p95=68ms, p99=185ms, avg gpu mem=25.9GB, kernel-switches=7
- 20 evictions/min: p50=22ms, p95=110ms, p99=340ms, avg gpu mem=28.3GB, kernel-switches=21, minor swap events=2

Observations from the snapshot:
- Median almost stable until ~20 evictions/min, after which p95/p99 explode. Matches hypothesis 1.
- Kernel-switch count correlates strongly with p95; when we see >10 switches/min we get big tail.
- Swap events (even minor) coincide with very large p99s — possibly blocking host-side memcpy. Need finer trace.

Quick sketch of next analysis steps:
- Correlate kernel-switch events to the allocation timeline (are we switching because a new kernel is chosen for a longer sequence length? or because quantization fallback triggers?). Add instrumentation to tag switch reason.
- Run the same across redwood-13b-q8 to see scaling with model size — expect threshold to be lower (fewer evictions needed to trigger tail)
- Test effect of enabling aggressive KV prefetch (speculative keep-alive) on tail — could mitigate but might increase steady mem footprint.

Questions / unknowns to resolve:
- Are kernel-switches caused primarily by sequence length variance or by allocator fragmentation? Need aligned counters (seq_len_histogram + allocator-frag metric).
- Is there a clear operational cutoff (evictions/min) that generalizes across models/quant profiles? Tentative cutoff: ~15–20 evictions/min for 7b quantized on A100-40. Verify on A10/RTX6000.
- Interaction with batching: when batching window increases, do tails smooth or worsen under eviction pressure? Add a small sweep for batch-window=[2,6,12] ms.

Data visualizations to produce (to attach later):
- thermometry curve: x-axis evictions/min, y-axis p95 and p99 (log-scale for p99)
- heatmap: kernel-switches per minute vs p95
- timeline: example 5-minute trace showing eviction timestamps aligned with mem high-water and individual request latencies (to show causal spikes)

Immediate TODOs (for me / quick):
- [ ] Add switch-reason tag in runtime telemetry (PR drafted: runtime/#2428) — ping Mateo for review.
- [ ] Run 5-run suite across redwood-13b-q8 on small pool (cost estimate: ~3 GPU-hours) — open infra ticket JIRA-INF-455
- [ ] Export traces to confluence page linked above and sketch final charts (Anika to help with plotting)

Notes to self (scratch):
- If swap events are frequent, maybe try pinning allocator pools per priority lane to reduce churn.
- Consider a cheap admission control: if eviction_rate>threshold then route new requests to smaller model variant or to dedicated cached lane. Add as canary policy in rollout config.

Slack refs:
- #runtime-telemetry thread: msg 1324 (Mateo) — suggests adding kernel-switch counters to trace span.
- #prod-deploys: quick note re: previous evictions during scale test 2025-09 (similar tail but looked like GC)

Rough conclusion (working):
- There is a sharp non-linear tail response to repeated small KV-cache evictions; operationally it's a useful signal (evictions/min) to trigger fallback routing. Need more runs across models and GPUs but the signal looks strong.

End of scratch notes. Will iterate after next 3-run suite (scheduled 2026-03-12 but postponed).

-- Erin
